answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% cost reduction; incumbent refuses price renegotiation, making negotiate_terms ineffective. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—directly applicable to meeting the 18% mandate. memory_c4 shows renegotiation can work but only when the vendor is willing; the incumbent's refusal closes that path. Deferring (memory_c5) or renewing (memory_c1) leave the cost mandate unmet. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses resilience but not cost pressure. With 14 days to contract expiry and no auto-renewal, switching is the only action that can deliver both cost compliance and contractual continuity. The 94% volume buffer is tight—this creates execution risk on onboarding speed and accuracy—but memory_c2's precedent of quick, accurate transition mitigates that. Standard_experiment scale allows monitoring of the new vendor's performance against our integration requirements before full reliance. Flag: if the low-cost vendor cannot scale to full demand or quality diverges, assembly line buffer becomes critical vulnerability. This decision trades some execution risk for cost compliance necessity.
